lessons.content:
Meet the language of the web.
Before creating beautiful websites, you need to understand
            the language that gives every webpage its structure.
            Welcome to your first step into HTML.

So, what exactly is HTML?
HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is the standard
        markup language used to create and structure content on the web.
        Think of it as the skeleton of a website.

HTML gives structure.
It tells the browser which content is a heading,
                    which content is a paragraph, where an image belongs,
                    and where a link should take the visitor.

Every website starts somewhere.
From simple blogs to massive online platforms, HTML helps
        organize the content users see and interact with.

Website Structure
Organize headings, paragraphs, sections, navigation and content.

Media & Content
Add images, videos, audio, links and other useful content.

Accessibility
Use meaningful elements to make content easier to understand and navigate.

How does HTML work?
You write HTML in a file. Your browser reads the markup
        and builds the webpage that appears on your screen.

Write HTML code
Create an HTML file and write elements such as headings, paragraphs and images.

Browser reads the code
The browser parses the HTML and understands the document structure.

Webpage appears
The browser renders the content so visitors can view and interact with it.

HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
Modern frontend development commonly uses three core technologies.
        Each one has a different responsibility.

HTML
Creates the structure and content of a webpage.

CSS
Controls the appearance, layout, colours and responsive design.

JavaScript
Adds behaviour, logic and interactivity to a webpage.

lessons.title: CNF/ | HTML Document Structure
headings: 1. Which element is the root of an HTML document?
2. Where is the visible webpage content placed?
3. What is the purpose of DOCTYPE?
lessons.content:
Inside an HTML document.
Every HTML webpage follows a document structure.
                Learn what happens behind the scenes, understand the
                important elements, and discover how browsers read your code.

Explore the anatomy of HTML

DOCTYPE Declaration
The DOCTYPE declaration tells the browser that this
                document uses modern HTML5 standards. It should be
                the first line of an HTML document.

Know the important building blocks.
These elements work together to create a properly structured
            HTML document.

The HTML Element
The root element of the page. All other HTML elements,
                except the DOCTYPE declaration, are placed inside it.

The Head Section
Contains document information such as the title,
                metadata, stylesheet links and other resources.

The Body Section
Contains the visible webpage content such as headings,
                paragraphs, images, buttons and links.

The Title Element
Defines the webpage title that usually appears in
                the browser tab and helps identify the page.

Why do we write DOCTYPE?
A small declaration makes a big difference in how the
            browser interprets your document.

Use HTML5 standards mode.
This declaration tells the browser to render the page
            using modern standards rather than an old compatibility
            or quirks mode. Place it at the very beginning of the file.

What does the browser display?
The head contains document information. The body contains
            the content that visitors see on the webpage.

Hello World!
Welcome to my first properly structured webpage.

Look at the difference.
The browser tab gets its title from the title element
                inside the head. The heading, paragraph and link are
                displayed because they are inside the body.
This separation keeps document information and visible
                content organized.

Build a complete HTML document.
This time, write the complete document structure yourself.
            Change the title, heading and paragraph, then run your code.

lessons.title: CNF/ | Links & Images
lessons.content: Connect ideas. Show the world. Links connect one page to another. Images bring visual meaning to your content. In this lesson, you will learn how to use both like a real web developer. A link is a doorway. The anchor element creates a clickable connection. Its href attribute tells the browser where that connection should lead. Meet the tag. The anchor tag wraps around text or another element. When a visitor clicks it, the browser follows the destination written inside the href attribute. Welcome to my website! Explore useful learning resources and discover something new. What's inside a URL? A URL is the address of a resource on the internet. Different parts help the browser locate the correct website and page. Example URL Go anywhere. An absolute URL contains the complete web address, including its protocol and domain. Move within your site. A relative URL points to a file or folder based on the current page's location. Understand a relative path If your current page is inside the pages folder, the link about.html points to another file in that same folder. Use ../ to move one folder level upward. Choose how a link opens. Stay in the same tab. This is the normal browser behaviour when no target attribute is specified. Open another tab. Use target="_blank" when you want the destination to open in a new tab. Turn information into visuals. The image element displays a picture on your webpage. It uses src for the image location and alt for a meaningful text alternative. Meet the tag. Unlike most HTML elements, img is a void element. It does not need a closing tag. Explore the outdoors A visual element can make a webpage more engaging and informative. src attribute Points to the image file or image URL. alt attribute Describes the image in text. Dimensions Width and height control displayed size. Describe what matters in the image instead of writing generic words like "photo". Make sure the image location is correct or the browser cannot load it. CSS such as max-width: 100% helps images fit smaller screens. Create a visual webpage. Try the code below. Change the link destination, image source, or alternative text and run your own example. ⌘ Link & Image Playground My Favourite Place Discover beautiful places around the world. Learning HTML is fun! lessons.content:
HTML Forms: Connect With Users.
Learn how websites collect information, create registration pages, build login forms and communicate with users through interactive HTML forms.

Create Your Account
Enter your details to get started.

What Are HTML Forms?
Imagine visiting a website and creating an account. You enter your name, email address and password. Then you click the Register button.
How does the website collect all this information? The answer is HTML Forms .
An HTML form is a section of a webpage that contains interactive controls. It allows users to enter information and submit it.

Login Forms
Collect usernames, emails and passwords to help users sign in.

Registration Forms
Collect information when someone creates a new account.

Contact Forms
Allow visitors to send questions and messages.

Search Forms
Allow users to search for products, articles or information.

Understanding the Form Element
The <form> element is the main container for form controls. Everything that belongs to a form is generally placed inside it.

CODE:
<form action="/submit" method="POST">
    <label for="username">Username:</label>
    <input type="text" id="username" name="username">
    <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>


How Does This Code Work?

<form>
Creates the form container.

<label>
Displays a description for the input field.

<input>
Allows the user to enter information.

<button>
Provides a button to submit the form.

Explore Input Types
The <input> element is one of the most important form elements. Its type attribute decides what kind of information a user can enter.
Input Type
Purpose
Common Use
text
Single-line text
Full name
email
Email address
Contact email
password
Hidden characters
Account password
number
Numeric value
Age or quantity
tel
Telephone number
Phone number
date
Date selection
Date of birth
time
Time selection
Appointment time
file
File selection
Document upload
checkbox
Independent choices
Select interests
radio
One choice in a group
Select one option
color
Color selection
Choose a theme color
range
Value slider
Volume control

CODE:
<input type="text" name="fullname">
<input type="email" name="email">
<input type="password" name="password">
<input type="date" name="birthday">
<input type="file" name="document">


Important Input Attributes
Attributes provide additional information and control the behaviour of form fields.

placeholder
Displays a hint inside an empty field.

value
Sets an initial value for a field.

required
Makes a field compulsory.

readonly
Prevents editing while keeping the value available for submission.

disabled
Disables the field and excludes it from form submission.

maxlength
Sets the maximum number of characters.

CODE:
<input
    type="text"
    name="fullname"
    placeholder="Enter your full name"
    maxlength="30"
    required
>


Why Are Labels Important?
A label tells the user what information belongs in a field. It also helps screen readers understand form controls.

CODE:
<label for="email">Email Address</label>
<input
    type="email"
    id="email"
    name="email"
    placeholder="you@example.com"
>

The for attribute of the label must match the id of the input.

More Than Just Input Fields
HTML offers additional elements to build flexible and useful forms.

1. Textarea
Use <textarea> when users need to enter longer text, such as feedback or a message.

CODE:
<textarea name="message" rows="5" cols="30">
</textarea>


2. Select and Option
Use <select> to create a dropdown list. Each choice is an <option> .

CODE:
<select name="course">
    <option value="html">HTML</option>
    <option value="css">CSS</option>
    <option value="javascript">JavaScript</option>
</select>


3. Radio Buttons
Radio buttons let users select one option from a group. Use the same name for the group.

CODE:
<input type="radio" name="level" value="beginner">
Beginner
<input type="radio" name="level" value="advanced">
Advanced


4. Checkboxes
Checkboxes allow users to select multiple independent choices.

CODE:
<input type="checkbox" name="skill" value="html">
HTML
<input type="checkbox" name="skill" value="css">
CSS


5. Fieldset and Legend
Use <fieldset> to group related form controls and <legend> to give that group a title.

CODE:
<fieldset>
    <legend>Personal Information</legend>
    <label for="student">Student Name</label>
    <input id="student" type="text">
</fieldset>


Validate User Information
Validation helps ensure users enter information in the expected format before a form is submitted.
Attribute
What It Does
required
Requires a value before submission.
minlength
Sets the minimum text length.
maxlength
Sets the maximum text length.
min
Sets the minimum numeric/date value.
max
Sets the maximum numeric/date value.
pattern
Checks text against a regular expression.

CODE:
<form>
    <input type="email" required>
    <input type="password" minlength="8" required>
    <input type="number" min="18" max="60">
    <button type="submit">Register</button>
</form>

lessons.content:
Colors & Backgrounds
Discover how colors create emotion, how backgrounds transform
        websites and how gradients make designs look modern.
        Let's turn simple pages into beautiful experiences.

How CSS Colors Work
CSS allows you to change the color of text, backgrounds,
        borders and almost every visible element.

What is a CSS Color?
A CSS color is a value that tells the browser which color
            should be displayed on an element. You can use color names,
            HEX values, RGB and HSL.

Color Names
Use predefined names like red, blue, tomato and cyan.

HEX Colors
Use hexadecimal codes such as #a855f7.

RGB Colors
Mix red, green and blue values to create colors.

CSS Background Properties
Background properties control what appears behind an element.

Background Color
The background-color property sets a solid color behind an element.

Background Image
You can use an image as the background of an element.

Background Repeat & Size

lessons.content:
Inside the Box Model.
Every HTML element is a box. Learn how content, padding,
            borders and margins work together to control the size
            and spacing of elements on a webpage.

BOX MODEL STRUCTURE

What is the CSS Box Model?
The CSS Box Model describes how every HTML element is displayed
        as a rectangular box.

Think of a cardboard box 📦
Imagine a product packed inside a cardboard box. The product
            is the content, the space around it is padding, the cardboard
            edge is the border and the outside gap between boxes is margin.
            CSS works in a similar way.

Content
The actual text, image or other material inside an element.

Padding
Space between the content and its border.

Border
The visible edge surrounding padding and content.

Margin
Space outside the border that separates elements.

Explore the Box Layers
The diagram shows how the four layers are arranged.
Outside → Inside: Margin → Border → Padding → Content

How to Use Each Property

Padding
Adds space inside an element, between its content and border.

Margin
Adds space outside an element, separating it from other elements.

Border
Creates an outline around the element.

Width & Height
Set the dimensions of the content area by default.

Understanding box-sizing
The box-sizing property controls how an element's total width
        and height are calculated.

content-box (Default)
With content-box, padding and border are added outside
            the specified width and height.

border-box
With border-box, padding and border are included inside
            the specified width and height.
This is a popular global setting because it makes layouts
            easier to calculate and control.

Build layouts with Flexbox & Grid.
Learn how to arrange elements, create responsive layouts,
            control alignment and build professional website structures.

Two powerful layout systems.
Flexbox and Grid are CSS layout systems. They help you position
        elements without using difficult floats or unnecessary positioning.

Flexbox
Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout system. It arranges
                elements in a row or a column. Use it for navigation bars,
                buttons, cards and aligning items.

CSS Grid
Grid is a two-dimensional layout system. It controls rows
                and columns together. Use it for galleries, dashboards
                and complete page layouts.

Flexbox vs Grid

Choose Flexbox
When you need to arrange items in one direction, such as

lessons.content:
One website. Every screen.
Learn how to make websites adapt to mobile phones, tablets
            and desktops. Build layouts that look beautiful on every device.

What is Responsive Design?
Responsive web design means creating websites that automatically
        adjust their layout, text, images and elements according to the
        screen size of the device being used.

Mobile
Small screens need compact navigation, readable text
                and content arranged mostly in a single column.

Tablet
Medium screens can show more content side by side,
                often using two-column layouts.

Desktop
Large screens provide more room for navigation,
                multi-column layouts and larger content sections.

The power of @media
CSS media queries let you apply different styles depending
            on the screen width or other device characteristics.

See the layout change.
Select a device below. The preview changes its layout to demonstrate
        how the same website can adapt to different screen sizes.

Responsive Preview Studio

Design your digital future.
A beautiful website for every screen.
Note: This is a visual demonstration of responsive layout
            behavior, not a real browser device emulator.

Three things to remember.

Flexible Widths
Use percentages, flexible grid units and max-width instead
                of forcing every element to have a fixed width.

Responsive Images
Images should scale inside their containers without
                overflowing or becoming distorted.

Viewport Meta Tag
This tag tells mobile browsers to use the device width
                as the page's viewport width.

Mobile-First Design
Start with a simple layout for small screens, then add
                more complex layouts for larger screens.

Animation vs Transition

        CSS animations can run through multiple stages using keyframes.

CSS Transitions
A transition smoothly changes a CSS property when a state
                changes, such as when a user hovers over a button.

CSS Animations

lessons.content:
Meet JavaScript. The Web's Logic.
Discover the programming language that makes websites interactive.
                Understand what JavaScript is, how it works with HTML and CSS,
                and why it is an essential part of modern web development.

What is JavaScript?
Understand the role of JavaScript in web development.
JavaScript is a programming language mainly
                used to make websites interactive and dynamic.
HTML creates the structure of a webpage, CSS controls its
                appearance, and JavaScript adds behavior and functionality.
For example, when you click a button and a menu opens,
                JavaScript can handle that interaction.

Interactive Websites
JavaScript responds to clicks, typing, scrolling and other user actions.

Dynamic Content
It can update webpage content without requiring the entire page to reload.

Application Logic
It handles calculations, conditions, data and the logic behind web applications.

HTML vs CSS vs JavaScript
Three technologies working together to build a webpage.

HTML
Creates headings, paragraphs, images, buttons and other webpage elements.

CSS
Controls colors, layouts, spacing, typography and visual appearance.

JavaScript
Adds interactions, calculations, animations and dynamic functionality.

Complete Website
All three technologies work together to create a functional webpage.

CODE:
<!-- HTML: Structure -->
<button id="myButton">Click Me</button>
<!-- CSS: Appearance -->
<style>
    button {
        background: blue;
        color: white;
        padding: 12px 20px;
    }
</style>
<!-- JavaScript: Behavior -->
<script>
    document.getElementById("myButton")
        .addEventListener("click", function() {
            alert("Hello, welcome!");
        });
</script>

HTML builds it. CSS styles it. JavaScript makes it interactive.

How JavaScript Works
Understand how your browser handles JavaScript code.
When a browser loads a webpage, it processes HTML,
                applies CSS and executes JavaScript.
JavaScript code is executed by a JavaScript engine .
                The engine reads and runs the instructions written by the developer.
Modern browsers include JavaScript engines that allow websites
                to respond to user actions and update content.

Browser Loads
The browser receives the webpage files.

Engine Reads
The JavaScript engine processes the code.

Code Executes
Instructions are executed by the engine.

Page Responds
The webpage can update and react to actions.

Open your browser's Developer Tools using F12,
                then select the Console tab. Your JavaScript
                console messages will appear there.

Where is JavaScript Used?
JavaScript is used in many areas of modern technology.

Web Development
Interactive websites, dashboards, forms and web applications.

Mobile Applications
Frameworks and tools can use JavaScript to build mobile applications.

Backend Development
Node.js allows JavaScript to run on servers and build backend systems.

Web Games
JavaScript can power browser games, animations and interactive experiences.

APIs & Data
JavaScript can communicate with APIs and work with data from servers.

Automation
It can automate repetitive tasks and perform useful programming operations.

Your First JavaScript Program
Learn how to write and execute a simple JavaScript instruction.
The console.log() method prints information

It is commonly used by developers to test code,

Common Beginner Mistakes
Understand a few mistakes you should avoid from the beginning.

Missing Quotation Marks
Text values need quotation marks. For example: console.log("Hello");

Incorrect Capitalization
JavaScript is case-sensitive. console.log() and Console.log() are not the same.

Misspelling Method Names
Use console.log() correctly. A spelling mistake can cause an error.

Ignoring Error Messages

Learn how JavaScript stores information, how variables work,
                    and how different data types help you build dynamic applications.

What Is a Variable?

                You can think of it as a labeled box where JavaScript keeps information
                that your program can use later.
For example, a website might store a user's name, age, email address,
                or whether someone is logged in. Variables make this information
                available whenever your code needs it.

Store Data
Variables keep information available inside your program.

Give It a Name
Every variable has an identifier that helps you access its value.

Use It Anywhere

Variable Value

lessons.content:
Make your code think.
Learn how JavaScript performs calculations, compares values,
            and makes decisions. This is where your code starts behaving
            intelligently.

What are operators?
Operators are special symbols that perform operations on values
                and variables. They help JavaScript calculate, compare and
                make decisions.

CODE:
let
price = 500;
let
quantity = 3;
let
total = price
*
quantity;

console.log(total);
// Output: 1500

In this example, the multiplication operator (*) multiplies
                price by quantity and stores the result in total.

Arithmetic operators
Arithmetic operators are used to perform mathematical
                calculations in JavaScript.

Comparison operators
Comparison operators compare two values and return a Boolean
                result: true or false.

CODE:
let
age = 18;

console.log(age >= 18);
// Output: true


Logical operators
Logical operators combine multiple conditions or reverse
                a condition.

CODE:
let
age = 20;
let
hasID = true;
let
allowed = age >= 18
&&
hasID;

console.log(allowed);
// Output: true


Operator laboratory
Change the values and operator. Run the calculation to see
                how JavaScript evaluates your expression.

Live calculation

Conditional statements
Conditions allow JavaScript to execute different blocks
                of code depending on whether a condition is true or false.

if statement
Executes a block of code when its condition is true.

else statement
Executes when the if condition is false.

else if statement
Checks another condition when previous conditions
                        are false.

switch statement
Selects one block from multiple possible cases.

CODE:
let
marks = 75;
if
(marks >= 80) {
    console.log("Excellent!");
}
else if
(marks >= 50) {
    console.log("You passed!");
}
else
{
    console.log("Try again!");
}
// Output: You passed!


CODE:
let
age = 19;
let
result = age >= 18
    ? "Adult"
    : "Minor";

console.log(result);
// Output: Adult

02. Which keyword sends a value back from a function?

lessons.content:
Write once. Run anywhere.
Functions make your code reusable, organized and powerful.
                Learn how to create your own instructions and make JavaScript
                perform tasks whenever you need them.

What is a Function?
Understand the idea before writing your first function.

A reusable block of code
A function is a block of code designed to perform a particular
                task. You write it once and call it whenever you need it.
                Instead of repeating the same code again and again, you can
                put that code inside a function.

Build your understanding
Explore the main ways to create and use functions in JavaScript.

Function Declaration
A function declaration creates a named function using the
                function keyword. You can call it by its name.

Parameters
Parameters are variables written inside the function
                parentheses. They receive values when the function runs.

Arguments
Arguments are the actual values you pass into a function
                when calling it.

The return Statement
Return sends a value back from a function. That value can
                be stored in a variable or used in another expression.

Arrow Functions
Arrow functions provide a shorter syntax for writing
                functions using the arrow symbol.

Function Expressions
A function expression stores a function inside a variable.
                It can then be called using that variable.

Inside a Function
Every part of a function has a purpose. Understand its structure.

CODE:
function
calculate
(a, b) {
let
result = a + b;
return
result;

}
// Function call
calculate
(10, 20);


Function vs Arrow Function
Both can perform tasks, but their syntax and behavior have differences.

Regular Function
Arrow Function

Uses arrow =>

            numbers and run your code.

Build a Function

Where can variables be used?
Scope determines where a variable can be accessed in your code.

Local Scope
A variable declared inside a function is generally
                accessible only inside that function.

Global Scope
A variable declared outside functions can usually be
                accessed throughout its accessible scope.

lessons.content:
Organize your data better.
Real applications work with collections of information.
            Learn how arrays store lists and objects organize related
            information into meaningful properties and values.

Why do we need data structures?
Understand why JavaScript needs arrays and objects to manage
            information efficiently.

Think like a developer.
Imagine building a student management system. You may
                need to store hundreds of student names, marks, emails
                and other details. Creating separate variables for
                every value would become difficult. Arrays and objects
                provide a structured way to manage that data.

Meet the Array
An array stores multiple values in a single variable.
            Each value has a position called an index.

Creating an Array
Square brackets are used to create an array. Values are
                separated by commas.

Accessing Array Values
Array indexing starts from zero. The first value is
                at index 0, not index 1.

How array indexes work
Each box represents one position in an array.
            The index tells JavaScript where a value is stored.

Work with Arrays
JavaScript provides built-in methods to add, remove,
            search and transform array values.

Runs a function for every array element.

Meet the Object
Objects store related information using key-value pairs.
            They are useful for describing real-world entities.

Student Object

What is an Object?
An object groups related properties together.
                Each property has a key and a value. You can access
                properties using dot notation or bracket notation.

More powerful object concepts
Objects can contain functions, other objects and nested data.

Object Methods
A function stored inside an object is commonly called
                a method.

Nested Objects
An object can contain another object as one of its
                property values.

Destructuring Arrays
Destructuring extracts values from an array into
                separate variables.

Object Destructuring
You can extract object properties into variables
                using their matching property names.

Array vs Object
Both store data, but they organize it differently.

Your website, your rules.
JavaScript can update this content without reloading the page.

What is the DOM?
The Document Object Model connects your HTML document
                with JavaScript.

Document Object Model
The DOM is a programming interface that represents an HTML
                    document as a tree of objects. JavaScript uses this structure
                    to access, modify, add, and remove elements on a webpage.
                    When a browser loads HTML, it creates a DOM tree that
                    JavaScript can interact with.

Understanding the DOM Tree
Every HTML element becomes a node in the DOM tree.
                Elements can have parent, child, and sibling relationships.

Selecting HTML Elements
JavaScript provides several methods to find elements
                inside the DOM.

Select by ID
Returns the element with the specified ID.

Select by Class
Returns a collection of elements with the same class.

Select by Tag
Finds elements using their HTML tag name.

First CSS Match
Returns the first element matching a CSS selector.

All CSS Matches
Returns all matching elements in a NodeList.

Access the Body
Provides direct access to the document body element.

Modifying DOM Elements
Once an element is selected, JavaScript can change its
                text, HTML, styles, and attributes.

01. Change Text
Use textContent to update the text inside an element.

02. Change HTML
Use innerHTML to read or replace HTML markup.
                    Only use trusted or safely handled content.

03. Change CSS
Update inline styles using the style property.

04. Change Attributes
Use setAttribute() to add or update HTML attributes.

Creating New Elements
JavaScript can create new HTML elements and insert them
                into the document.

Create an Element
createElement() creates a new HTML element in memory.

Add it to the Page
appendChild() inserts a node inside another element.

JavaScript Events
Events allow JavaScript to respond when users interact
                with a webpage.

click
Triggered when an element is clicked.

mouseover
Triggered when the pointer enters an element.

keydown
Triggered when a keyboard key is pressed.

submit
Triggered when a form is submitted.

change
Triggered when a form control value changes.

input
Triggered when the value of an input changes.

load
Triggered when a resource or page finishes loading.

dblclick
Triggered when an element is double-clicked.

Event Listeners
addEventListener() attaches an event handler to an element.
                    It lets you run a function when a particular event occurs.

JavaScript Beyond the Now.
Learn how JavaScript handles tasks that take time.
            Understand Promises, async/await, API requests and
            build your own asynchronous product loader.

What is Asynchronous JavaScript?
Not every operation finishes instantly. Async JavaScript helps
            your application stay responsive while waiting for results.

Synchronous
Code runs one statement at a time. The next statement waits
                until the current operation finishes.

Asynchronous
Some operations can complete later while JavaScript continues
                executing other available work.

Non-blocking
Long-running tasks such as network requests can happen without
                freezing the entire page.

Synchronous example

Asynchronous example

Promises
A Promise represents the eventual result of an asynchronous operation.

Three Promise states
Pending: The operation is still running.
Fulfilled: The operation completed successfully.
Rejected: The operation failed.

Promise methods
Method
Purpose
then()
Runs when a Promise is fulfilled.
catch()
Handles a rejected Promise.
finally()
Runs after the Promise settles, either way.
Promise.all()
Waits for all supplied Promises to fulfill, or rejects if one rejects.

Async & Await
Async and await make Promise-based code easier to read and organize.

async keyword
Adding async before a function
                makes that function return a Promise.

await keyword
await pauses the execution of
                its surrounding async function until the Promise settles.

The Event Loop
See how JavaScript coordinates synchronous code, asynchronous callbacks and the event loop.

Execution sequence

questions.question: Which operator gives the remainder after division?
questions.explanation: The modulo operator % returns the remainder.

questions.question: Which method displays a message in the browser console?
questions.explanation: console.log() writes information to the browser developer console.

questions.question: Which loop runs at least once before checking its condition?
questions.explanation: A do...while loop checks its condition after the first execution.

questions.question: What does break do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: break immediately exits the nearest enclosing loop or switch.

questions.question: Which method adds an item to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: push() adds one or more elements to the end of an array.

questions.question: How do you access the first item in an array called colors?
questions.explanation: JavaScript arrays use zero-based indexing.

questions.question: Which syntax accesses an object's name property?
questions.explanation: Dot notation accesses an object's property.

questions.question: Which method selects an element using a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: document.querySelector() returns the first matching element.

questions.question: Which method attaches an event listener?
questions.explanation: addEventListener() registers a function to run when an event occurs.

questions.question: What does textContent change?
questions.explanation: textContent gets or sets the text content of an element.

questions.question: Which keyword sends a value back from a function?
questions.explanation: return ends a function and optionally sends a value back.

questions.question: What does continue do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: continue skips the remaining statements in the current iteration.

questions.question: What does an async function always return?
questions.explanation: An async function always returns a Promise.

questions.question: Which keyword waits for a Promise to settle?
questions.explanation: await pauses the surrounding async function until the Promise settles.

questions.question: Which method handles a rejected Promise?
questions.explanation: catch() handles a rejection in a Promise chain.

questions.question: What does fetch() commonly return?
questions.explanation: fetch() returns a Promise that fulfills with a Response object.

questions.question: Which block is used with try to handle errors?
questions.explanation: The catch block handles errors thrown inside the try block.

questions.question: What does response.json() do?
questions.explanation: response.json() reads the response body and parses it as JSON.

questions.question: Which Promise method waits for all supplied Promises to fulfill?
questions.explanation: Promise.all() fulfills when all input Promises fulfill.

questions.question: Which queue generally has priority over timer callbacks after synchronous code finishes?
questions.explanation: Promise reactions are microtasks and generally run before timer tasks.

questions.question: Does fetch() reject automatically for an HTTP 404 response?
questions.explanation: fetch() normally fulfills for HTTP error responses. Check response.ok.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of finally() in a Promise chain?
questions.explanation: finally() runs after settlement whether the Promise fulfilled or rejected.
